scenes.text: The dragon's accountant is hiding inside a fireproof biscuit tin. Outside it: one mountain of receipts and a smaller mountain of former accountants.

choices.label: Sort the receipts by scorch mark
choices.hint: Success keeps evidence for the audit.
choices.win: The biscuit tin opens. A tiny hand gives you a labelled folder.
choices.lose: You classify three receipts as toast. They were essential toast.

onWin.memory: You rescued the dragon's receipts from the biscuit-tin accountant.

choices.label: Buy the accountant's emergency duplicate
choices.hint: Keep the receipts and unlock a finale approach.
choices.win: His emergency duplicate was under the emergency biscuits.
choices.lose: The biscuit tin remains firmly shut.

onWin.memory: You paid fifteen gold for the dragon accountant's emergency duplicate.

choices.label: Carry the whole mountain to the tax office
choices.win: You carry a taxable mountain. The dragon calls this a capital improvement.
choices.lose: The mountain catches fire. The accountant changes tins.

onWin.memory: You carried a dragon's entire filing mountain.

onLose.memory: The dragon's receipts burned during your attempt to lift them.

scenes.text: The auditor finds a deduction for 'one emotionally necessary village'. You have the receipts. Regrettably, so does the village.

choices.label: Reclassify the village as dependent relatives
choices.win: The auditor accepts. The dragon acquires four hundred dependants and a school newsletter.
choices.lose: The village requests pocket money. The auditor requests your head.

onWin.memory: You registered an entire village as the dragon's dependants.

choices.label: Have the dragon apologise to the village
choices.win: It is a very large apology. The village accepts payment in roofing.
choices.lose: The apology starts with 'if anyone was offended'. The village objects.

onWin.memory: You negotiated replacement roofs for the dragon's village.

scenes.text: Without receipts, the auditor wants a demonstration of 'ordinary business expenses'. The dragon has prepared an ordinary business knight.

choices.label: Explain depreciation before the knight ignites
choices.win: The knight depreciates gracefully. Into retirement, alive.
choices.lose: The dragon hears 'appreciation'. It appreciates the knight flambé.

onWin.memory: Your lecture on depreciation saved the business knight.

onLose.memory: The tax demonstration ended in knight flambé.

choices.label: Stand between the knight and accounting
choices.win: Your singed outline is accepted as documentary evidence.
choices.lose: You discover that tax liability can be measured in burns.

onWin.memory: You became the dragon's documentary evidence.

finaleChoices.label: Submit the fireproof duplicate with everything itemised
finaleChoices.win: Every deduction has a receipt. The dragon gets a refund and buys the accountant a larger tin.
finaleChoices.lose: The refund is approved in copper. Delivery crushes the desk.

onWin.memory: The fireproof duplicate won the dragon a tax refund.

scenes.text: The lich's tenancy agreement predates the kingdom. A skeleton in slippers asks whether you have an appointment or an appointment-shaped weapon.

choices.label: Read the nine-hundred-year break clause
choices.win: The lease permits eviction only if he gets his deposit back. The slippers nod.
choices.lose: You accidentally renew him for another dynasty.

onWin.memory: You discovered that the lich is owed nine centuries of deposit interest.

choices.label: Fund a moving van with reinforced soul storage
choices.hint: Negotiate a move instead of a siege.
choices.win: The skeleton starts packing. All the boxes say 'fragile: mortal remains'.
choices.lose: No van is available.

onWin.memory: You paid for the lich's moving van.

choices.label: Take the front door off its hinges
choices.win: You serve notice directly through the new architectural feature.
choices.lose: The door is a beloved ancestor. The family assembles.

onLose.memory: You insulted the lich's ancestor, who was also his front door.

scenes.text: The lich agrees to leave if you find a flat accepting pets. His pet is the basement. It has started following you.

choices.label: Write a flattering reference for the basement
choices.win: 'Quiet, self-contained, eats damp.' A landlord is delighted.
choices.lose: The basement eats the reference and one supporting wall.

onWin.memory: You found a pet-friendly flat for a sentient basement.

choices.label: Teach it to stay
choices.win: Good basement. Very good basement. The lich cries one dust.
choices.lose: It sits. On your foot.

onWin.memory: The lich's basement now responds to 'stay'.

scenes.text: A row of identical jam jars blocks the stairs. One contains the lich's soul. The others contain his frankly excessive marmalade.

choices.label: Identify the jar that fears the tenancy tribunal
choices.win: The soul rattles. Marmalade, famously, does not fear due process.
choices.lose: You threaten the apricot preserve. It retains counsel.

onWin.memory: You identified the lich's soul by its fear of the tenancy tribunal.

choices.label: Carry every jar outside without tasting any
choices.win: The soul and the preserves reach the pavement intact.
choices.lose: You drop one. Citrus revenge follows.

onWin.memory: You moved a lich's entire marmalade collection.

scenes.text: The royal laundry basket requests witness protection. It saw the left sock leave willingly, carrying a tiny suitcase.

choices.label: Promise the basket a new identity
choices.win: It becomes a humble bread bin and gives you the sock's forwarding address.
choices.lose: You call it 'Basket Two'. It withdraws cooperation.

onWin.memory: The royal laundry basket entered witness protection as a bread bin.

choices.label: Purchase the sock's train ticket records
choices.hint: Follow the sock into the labour movement.
choices.win: One single to Freedom, changing at Damp Junction.
choices.lose: The station is closed.

onWin.memory: You bought evidence that the royal sock fled by train.

choices.label: Search the royal drawer without breathing
choices.win: You recover a left-shaped indent and a revolutionary pamphlet.
choices.lose: A century of royal foot announces itself.

onLose.memory: The royal drawer defeated your lungs.

scenes.text: The sock is organising the kingdom's neglected left things. A left glove asks if you are management. A left shoe blocks the exit.

choices.label: Draft a five-day footwear week
choices.win: The shoe moves aside. The sock agrees to one final audience.
choices.lose: You forgot weekends. The glove calls a general strike.

onWin.memory: You negotiated a five-day footwear week with the runaway sock.

choices.label: Listen without calling anyone odd
choices.win: For once, someone hears their side. Their left side.
choices.lose: You say 'all right'. The meeting takes it personally.

onWin.memory: You heard the left things' grievances without making the obvious joke.

scenes.text: Your only lead is a drawer that locks from inside. It is sheltering the sock's replacement, a nervous knitted turnip.

choices.label: Convince the turnip to act naturally
choices.win: It practises being worn. Unsettlingly convincing.
choices.lose: It photosynthesises under questioning.

onWin.memory: You coached a turnip to impersonate a royal sock.

choices.label: Follow the loose thread under the door
choices.win: The thread leads to a secret knitting cell.
choices.lose: The thread leads out of your own trousers.

onWin.memory: A loose thread led you to a secret knitting cell.

finaleChoices.label: Offer the sock its negotiated footwear contract
finaleChoices.win: The sock returns on union terms. The king must now wash his own feet.
finaleChoices.lose: The king signs with his right hand. Talks briefly collapse.

onWin.memory: The king accepted union terms for his left sock.

scenes.text: Both armies call a ceasefire to inspect your sandwich. One claims the mustard is a provocation. The other has mobilised a pickle division.

choices.label: Declare the sandwich a neutral state
choices.win: They recognise its borders. The crust gains diplomatic immunity.
choices.lose: Both armies appoint ambassadors. Neither will leave the bag.

onWin.memory: You secured diplomatic immunity for a sandwich.

choices.label: Pay the official bread corridor toll
choices.hint: Guaranteed passage, but the lunch loses its military prestige.
choices.win: A drummer announces the transit of one extremely important lunch.
choices.lose: The bread corridor is closed.

onWin.memory: You paid a bread-corridor toll to move lunch through a war.

choices.label: Sprint between the catapults without spilling soup
choices.win: You clear the battlefield. The soup has acquired a medal.
choices.lose: A crouton causes an international incident.

onWin.memory: Your lunch sprint earned the soup a military medal.

onLose.memory: A crouton from your delivery caused an international incident.

scenes.text: The soup whispers through a straw: 'My name is Gregory. I have dependants. Mostly croutons.' The waiter approaches with a pepper mill.

choices.label: Disguise Gregory as a decorative pond
choices.win: A tiny reed conceals him beautifully. The croutons practise being ducks.
choices.lose: The waiter asks why the pond smells of lunch.

onWin.memory: You disguised Gregory the soup as a duck pond.

choices.label: Buy Gregory and declare him takeaway
choices.hint: Avoid the kitchen; keep Gregory's disguise.
choices.win: Gregory objects to being bought, then notices the exit.
choices.lose: The till refuses.

onWin.memory: You bought Gregory's freedom as a takeaway order.

choices.label: Lift the entire table and walk out
choices.win: A table for one becomes a vehicle for six bowls.
choices.lose: The legs fold. The waiter applauds your reservation cancellation.

onWin.memory: You used restaurant furniture as a soup getaway vehicle.

scenes.text: At the exit, Gregory's crouton children demand to rescue their uncle. Uncle is garlic bread and has no opinion on the matter.

choices.label: Smuggle Uncle in your sleeve
choices.win: The family is reunited. Your sleeve is wonderfully fragrant.
choices.lose: Butter betrays you at the elbow.

onWin.memory: You rescued Gregory's garlic-bread uncle.

choices.label: Explain that Uncle may be happier here
choices.win: A mature conversation. Gregory leaves him a forwarding napkin.
choices.lose: The croutons demand custody mediation.

onWin.memory: Gregory left his garlic-bread uncle a forwarding napkin.

scenes.text: The chef corners you beside a tureen. Gregory pretends to be normal soup. He is doing this by shouting 'ordinary soup noises'.

choices.label: Distract the chef with a fabricated inspection
choices.win: You condemn the ladle. Gregory escapes during the appeal.
choices.lose: The chef requests credentials. Gregory says 'blub'.

onWin.memory: You condemned a ladle to help Gregory escape.

choices.label: Drink the decoy soup without flinching
choices.win: Entirely ordinary. Gregory is deeply offended by your satisfied expression.
choices.lose: The decoy contains experimental chilli.

onLose.memory: Experimental chilli nearly ended Gregory's rescue.

scenes.text: The goblins demand dental cover. Their dark lord offers a dental cover: one enormous helmet. The meeting is entering its fourth headbutt.

choices.label: Calculate the cost of replacing every headbutted manager
choices.win: Dental insurance is cheaper. The helmet becomes a suggestion box.
choices.lose: The dark lord introduces a headbutt tax.

onWin.memory: You proved dental insurance costs less than headbutted managers.

choices.label: Contribute to the goblin strike fund
choices.hint: Stand with the workers; unlock collective bargaining.
choices.win: They give you a tiny placard and an enormous responsibility.
choices.lose: The fund is closed.

onWin.memory: You funded the goblins' strike and carried their placard.

choices.label: Demonstrate a safer headbutt on the table
choices.win: The table joins the union. It has endured enough.
choices.lose: The table wins. Management applauds.

onWin.memory: A table joined the goblin union after your demonstration.

scenes.text: Your new comrades ask you to lead the chant. Their current slogan is 'LESS DYING, PLEASE', which tested well across all departments.

choices.label: Lead a chant with a legally actionable rhyme
choices.win: The dark lord comes out to negotiate before the second verse.
choices.lose: You rhyme 'pension' with 'dismemberment'. The meter collapses.

onWin.memory: Your legally actionable chant brought the dark lord to the table.

choices.label: Hold the line against the skeleton scabs
choices.win: You point out skeletons also lack dental cover. They swap sides.
choices.lose: Their picket line has significantly more elbows.

onWin.memory: The skeleton strikebreakers joined the dental-cover campaign.

scenes.text: Payroll has been replaced by an enchanted sack that screams whenever a goblin earns overtime. The sack is also requesting a break.

choices.label: Audit the screaming sack
choices.win: The sack has been withholding its own wages. A difficult meeting follows.
choices.lose: The sack alleges you are an expense and attempts to swallow you.

onWin.memory: You discovered the payroll sack was withholding its own wages.

choices.label: Counsel the sack through a breathing exercise
choices.win: The screaming stops. The payslips emerge with little apology notes.
choices.lose: It inhales you instead.

onWin.memory: You taught the payroll sack to breathe before processing overtime.

finaleChoices.label: Present the workers' signed collective agreement
finaleChoices.win: Dental cover, lunch breaks, no unpaid hauntings. The dark lord signs in washable blood.
finaleChoices.lose: He signs, then disputes the lunch definition. Lawyers arrive.

onWin.memory: You won the goblins a signed collective agreement.

scenes.text: The hellhound's heads vote on the route. Two want the park. One wants to consume a cathedral. The duchess says they are usually so democratic.

choices.label: Negotiate a park with a small chapel
choices.win: A workable compromise. The chapel can be rebuilt.
choices.lose: The third head invokes the constitution. It is written in fire.

onWin.memory: You negotiated a hellhound walking route with optional small chapel.

choices.label: Buy three separate distraction sausages
choices.hint: All heads stay occupied; the finale still needs handling.
choices.win: Each head assumes it received the largest sausage. Peace through geometry.
choices.lose: No sausages remain.

onWin.memory: Three geometrically ambiguous sausages saved a cathedral.

choices.label: Hold the lead through a squirrel sighting
choices.win: The squirrel withdraws from public life. You retain both arms.
choices.lose: For several streets you are the dog walk.

onWin.memory: You held a hellhound back from a squirrel.

onLose.memory: The hellhound dragged you through several streets.

scenes.text: The overdue book insists the library is late collecting it. Its margins contain three centuries of increasingly personal legal arguments.

choices.label: Find the original return receipt in the margins
choices.win: A receipt! The book had been using it as a character witness.
choices.lose: The margin cross-examines you until you forget your name.

onWin.memory: You found a return receipt inside a book's legal argument.

choices.label: Pay for a retrospective renewal
choices.hint: Earn a hearing instead of being sent through the stacks.
choices.win: Your renewal is backdated to a kingdom that no longer exists.
choices.lose: Renewals are closed.

onWin.memory: You renewed the library book retroactively by three centuries.

choices.label: Ignore its arguments and carry it inside
choices.win: It quotes precedent all the way. You develop a useful immunity to footnotes.
choices.lose: It opens on a really sharp footnote.

onWin.memory: You carried a litigious book through three centuries of footnotes.

scenes.text: A jury of dictionaries hears your case. The thesaurus keeps saying 'objection, protest, dissent, remonstrance'.

choices.label: Define 'overdue' narrowly enough to fit the receipt
choices.win: The dictionaries accept the definition. The thesaurus has no words. Briefly.
choices.lose: You are found guilty of lexical opportunism.

onWin.memory: A jury of dictionaries accepted your definition of overdue.

choices.label: Appeal to the children's section
choices.win: A picture book supplies a simple moral. The dictionaries feel ashamed.
choices.lose: The moral is 'never trust strangers with fines'.

onWin.memory: A picture book shamed the library's dictionary jury.

scenes.text: The returns chute drops you into Reference. A librarian whispers that nobody leaves Reference without becoming a source.

choices.label: Catalogue your own escape under E
choices.win: A perfect filing loophole. Your escape is now available in hardback.
choices.lose: You are cross-referenced under Trapped, see Also: Fool.

onWin.memory: You catalogued your library escape under E.

choices.label: Crawl beneath the silent biographies
choices.win: One biography mouths 'good luck'. You decline to find out whose.
choices.lose: You sneeze in a volume of famous last words.

onWin.memory: A silent biography wished you luck beneath the library shelves.

finaleChoices.label: Cite the dictionary jury's acquittal
finaleChoices.win: The fine is struck out. The book begins writing its courtroom memoir.
finaleChoices.lose: The acquittal has itself accrued an overdue charge.

onWin.memory: You defeated the library fine with a dictionary jury's acquittal.

scenes.text: The instructions show a smiling stick figure assembling a wardrobe with twelve hands. You have fewer hands and considerably less optimism.

choices.label: Decipher the wordless stick-figure theology
choices.win: You discover step one means 'do not build during a thunderstorm'. Useful, belatedly.
choices.lose: Step one means 'summon assistance'. You summon a hinge demon.

onWin.memory: You translated twelve-handed furniture instructions.

choices.label: Hire twelve goblin hands, attached to six goblins
choices.hint: Guarantee the opening assembly; owe the crew a recommendation.
choices.win: The crew arrives wearing tiny hard hats. One is the foreman and has no hands.
choices.lose: The crew is unavailable.

onWin.memory: You hired a six-goblin furniture crew and their handless foreman.

choices.label: Bend the panels until they resemble a wardrobe
choices.win: The wardrobe fits through the door. Technically, you made the door fit.
choices.lose: You invent flat-pack shrapnel.

onLose.memory: Your furniture technique produced flat-pack shrapnel.

scenes.text: There is one spare screw. The wardrobe says it is important. The giant asks why the wardrobe can speak. Neither is in the instructions.

choices.label: Ask the wardrobe which screw it is missing
choices.win: It indicates its conscience. You fit the screw. It apologises for the shouting.
choices.lose: It requests a private consultation with the hinge demon.

onWin.memory: You installed the wardrobe's conscience using the spare screw.

choices.label: Perform the load test yourself
choices.win: You survive inside a wardrobe sitting inside another wardrobe. Certified.
choices.lose: The wardrobe decides you are a coat.

onWin.memory: You personally certified a giant's nesting wardrobes.

scenes.text: The dark lord's nephew wants a bedtime story in which the moon gets eaten. The moon is visible through the window and listening anxiously.

choices.label: Tell a story where the moon negotiates a smaller bite
choices.win: The child agrees to a crescent. The moon takes notes for its lawyer.
choices.lose: The child asks for a practical demonstration.

onWin.memory: You promised the dark lord's nephew a story with only a crescent-sized bite.

choices.label: Replace the moon with a cheese wheel
choices.win: A convincing lunar eclipse. The nephew requests crackers.
choices.lose: The moon complains that the cheese is a poor likeness.

onWin.memory: You impersonated the moon using a cheese wheel.

choices.label: Purchase the officially licensed sleep spell
choices.hint: Preparation +1 for the finale; side effects include dreams about licensing.
choices.win: The spell arrives with seventeen pages of terms and a tiny pillow.
choices.lose: The spell is out of stock.

onWin.memory: You bought a licensed sleep spell with seventeen pages of terms.

scenes.text: The monster under the bed hands you its resignation. It cannot work with a child who keeps asking it for career advice.

choices.label: Coach the monster through an exit interview
choices.win: It stays on a consultancy basis. The nephew respects the title.
choices.lose: The nephew offers it an unpaid internship. It bites the contract.

onWin.memory: The bedtime monster now works as a consultant.

choices.label: Take over under-bed duties until lights out
choices.win: You make one convincing growl. The child finally brushes his teeth.
choices.lose: There is another monster under the monster. It wants your CV.

onWin.memory: You covered the under-bed monster's shift.

scenes.text: The tower asks a security question: 'What was your first familiar's maiden name?' The wizard insists it was a snail, and a very private snail.

choices.label: Trace the snail's wedding announcement
choices.win: Snail Society, volume four. The wedding was three inches from the birthplace.
choices.lose: The announcement is still travelling to the printer.

onWin.memory: You located a wizard's snail familiar through its society wedding announcement.

choices.label: Bribe the tower's helpdesk gargoyle
choices.hint: Reach the snail verification step.
choices.win: The gargoyle escalates you to someone technically alive.
choices.lose: The gargoyle is on lunch.

onWin.memory: A helpdesk gargoyle escalated your password ticket to someone alive.

choices.label: Climb past the login window
choices.win: You bypass authentication using a drainpipe. Security hates this one trick.
choices.lose: The drainpipe requests a verification code.

onLose.memory: A drainpipe locked you out for failing two-factor authentication.

scenes.text: The tower sends a one-time code to the snail. You can see the snail. You can also see it beginning a long and thoughtful turn.

choices.label: Read the code in its trail before it expires
choices.win: Correct on the first attempt. It was six zeroes and a leaf.
choices.lose: The trail spells 'loading'. You have been misled.

onWin.memory: You decoded two-factor authentication from a snail trail.

choices.label: Convince the tower that patience is secure
choices.win: It extends the timeout to geological time. Sensible for a snail.
choices.lose: It classifies you as suspiciously patient.

onWin.memory: The wizard's tower now supports geological-time login codes.

scenes.text: Too many attempts. The tower has locked itself out of itself. It asks you to click every picture containing a smaller tower.

choices.label: Solve the architectural identity crisis
choices.win: You explain that a turret can be part of a tower. It weeps stone tears.
choices.lose: It decides you are a smaller tower and tries to absorb you.

onWin.memory: You talked a locked-out tower through an architectural identity crisis.

choices.label: Offer emotional support without accepting cookies
choices.win: The tower calms down. You retain control of your browsing preferences.
choices.lose: It offers actual cookies. They are masonry.

onWin.memory: You comforted a wizard's tower without accepting its cookies.

scenes.text: The seating chart puts the bride's ex next to the garlic fountain. The best man says this is a coincidence, then asks if you brought a mop.

choices.label: Rearrange six centuries of grudges
choices.win: Everyone sits beside someone they have only moderately murdered.
choices.lose: You seat an ancestral feud beside another ancestral feud. They reconnect.

onWin.memory: You arranged a vampire wedding by degrees of ancestral murder.

choices.label: Pay to replace the garlic fountain with beetroot
choices.hint: Save the ex; gain an ally for the reception.
choices.win: The ex is grateful. The beetroot is delighted by its promotion.
choices.lose: The supplier has departed.

onWin.memory: You saved the vampire bride's ex with a beetroot fountain.

choices.label: Carry the fountain into the sunlight yourself
choices.win: A clean removal. Several guests leave appreciative scorch marks.
choices.lose: The fountain has an aggressive splash radius.

onLose.memory: The garlic fountain splashed you during the vampire wedding.

scenes.text: The best man's toast begins 'I remember her first husband'. There were forty-seven. He has brought slides.

choices.label: Catch the projector cable with your foot
choices.win: A tactful technical failure. The bride silently names you in her will.
choices.lose: The cable was a guest's tail. The slideshow continues during the fight.

onWin.memory: You ended a forty-seven-husband wedding slideshow with a discreet cable tug.

choices.label: Deliver a better toast before slide two
choices.win: You focus on their future. This may be eternal, but you keep it to a minute.
choices.lose: Your opening line is 'til death do you part'. An awkward room.

onWin.memory: Your one-minute wedding toast displaced forty-seven dead husbands.

scenes.text: The plumber has accidentally become six. His apprenticeship paperwork says he will qualify in seventeen years. His toolbox is already judging you.

choices.label: Translate his finger-paint plumbing diagram
choices.win: The blue blob is a temporal valve. The green blob is his mum.
choices.lose: You open his mum. Metaphorically. The toolbox disapproves.

onWin.memory: A six-year-old plumber's finger painting revealed the temporal valve.

choices.label: Hire the plumber's future qualified self
choices.hint: Get the valve map; create a very awkward family meeting.
choices.win: He arrives, grounds himself, and hands over a diagram.
choices.lose: His future self is unavailable.

onWin.memory: You hired a future plumber who promptly grounded his six-year-old self.

choices.label: Hold the pipe shut until adulthood returns
choices.win: The leak stops. You briefly remember a retirement you have not earned.
choices.lose: Your arms experience puberty in opposite directions.

onLose.memory: The Fountain of Youth gave your arms incompatible ages.

scenes.text: A blockage of discarded birthdays has flooded Tuesday. An elderly toddler asks whether you are here yesterday or just badly organised.

choices.label: Sort the birthdays into chronological order
choices.win: Tuesday drains. Everyone gets one appropriate-sized slice of cake.
choices.lose: You put Leap Day first. An extra Tuesday appears.

onWin.memory: You drained Tuesday by sorting discarded birthdays.

choices.label: Wade upstream without remembering your own birth
choices.win: You reach the valve before the flashback. A merciful omission.
choices.lose: You remember it. You were cross then, too.

onWin.memory: You reached the time valve without witnessing your own birth.

scenes.text: The prize marrow has slipped you a note: 'I grew myself. The farmer did nothing.' The farmer quietly offers you a smaller marrow full of coins.

choices.label: Interview the marrow independently
choices.win: It supplies photographic evidence, including a humiliating watering-can incident.
choices.lose: It demands anonymity. It is the only twenty-foot marrow in the village.

onWin.memory: The prize marrow testified against its farmer.

choices.label: Buy the coin marrow as evidence
choices.hint: Keep the bribe off the judging table.
choices.win: Evidence secured. Lunch secured. Fiscal policy surprisingly edible.
choices.lose: The exhibit has been sold.

onWin.memory: You purchased an evidence marrow filled with attempted bribery.

choices.label: Lift the prize marrow to check for hidden supports
choices.win: Entirely self-supporting. It flexes a leaf, smugly.
choices.lose: It asks to put you down for a moment. It does so from a height.

onLose.memory: The prize marrow demonstrated its strength by dropping you.

scenes.text: The kraken has booked the shallow end. It occupies the whole shallow end, most of the deep end, and the lifeguard's increasingly small office.

choices.label: Design a floatation aid for eight embarrassed arms
choices.win: Eight armbands, one dignity-preserving cape. It relaxes.
choices.lose: Your prototype is technically a net. It has strong feelings about nets.

onWin.memory: You designed a dignity-preserving swimming cape for a kraken.

choices.label: Book a private lesson without spectators
choices.hint: Protect its confidence; earn a calmer finale approach.
choices.win: The lifeguard clears the pool. The pool itself thanks you.
choices.lose: The pool is fully booked.

onWin.memory: You funded a private swimming lesson for an embarrassed kraken.

choices.label: Demonstrate breathing without showing off
choices.win: You inhale. You exhale. The kraken applauds eight times.
choices.lose: You swallow a mouthful. It cancels the demonstration on your behalf.

onWin.memory: Your modest breathing demonstration won eight rounds of kraken applause.

scenes.text: Other krakens arrive to watch. Your student tries to hide behind a pool noodle. Only one inch of it is hidden, but that inch is committed.

choices.label: Recruit the onlookers as an encouraging wave machine
choices.win: They cheer in eight-part harmony. Your student emerges from the inch.
choices.lose: They do a Mexican wave. It becomes a local weather event.

onWin.memory: You turned mocking krakens into an eight-part cheering section.

choices.label: Float beside the pool noodle and wait
choices.win: Eventually, another inch lets go. It is a start.
choices.lose: The pool noodle asks you to stop leaning on it emotionally.

onWin.memory: You waited quietly beside a kraken's determined pool noodle.

finaleChoices.label: Use the private lesson's one-arm-at-a-time routine
finaleChoices.win: One arm, then two, then eight. The cape is unnecessary now. It keeps it anyway.
finaleChoices.lose: Eight arms choose eight directions. You are the meeting point.

onWin.memory: The kraken learned to swim and kept its dignity cape.

scenes.text: The Parade of Snails has reached the first kerb. The marshal announces a brief six-hour pause. A snail asks you to post its resignation ahead of it.

choices.label: Find a level route that avoids the salt merchant
choices.win: A safe detour. The salt merchant calls you anti-business.
choices.lose: Your detour crosses a crisp factory's loading bay.

onWin.memory: You rerouted the snail parade away from a salt merchant.

choices.label: Hire a very small wagon for the first kerb
choices.hint: Save time; the snails insist it still counts as walking.
choices.win: Four hundred passengers, one modest axle. A historic ascent.
choices.lose: The wagon is unavailable.

onWin.memory: A tiny wagon carried four hundred snails over their first kerb.

choices.label: Carry the marshal until morale improves
choices.win: He thanks you in a speech that lasts until tomorrow.
choices.lose: He has a very heavy ceremonial shell.

onWin.memory: You carried the snail marshal through his day-long thank-you speech.

scenes.text: Rain arrives. The snails are delighted until they discover the puddle has organised a rival parade and is claiming the route.

choices.label: Merge the parades without dissolving the committee
choices.win: Snails lead, puddle follows. The route becomes temporarily scenic.
choices.lose: The puddle insists on equal shell representation.

onWin.memory: You negotiated a joint snail-and-puddle parade.

choices.label: Hold an umbrella over all four hundred marchers
choices.win: An impossible stretch of arms. The snails chant your name very slowly.
choices.lose: Your umbrella is declared an unauthorised venue.

onWin.memory: Four hundred snails chanted your name beneath one umbrella.

scenes.text: Backstage, your rival is rehearsing a victory speech into a hairbrush. The trophy engraver has sensibly left both names in pencil.

choices.label: Call in the truce you made on the road
choices.hint: Unlock a shared-trophy ending.
choices.win: The hairbrush lowers. For once, you are both off script.
choices.lose: Your rival declines.

onWin.memory: Your rival agreed to honour the road truce at the showdown.

choices.label: Find the page of rules that forbids pre-written speeches
choices.win: Rule 43. Your rival quietly eats page one.
choices.lose: The page is an advertisement for your rival's memoir.

onWin.memory: You challenged your rival's pre-written victory speech under Rule 43.

choices.label: Warm up by lifting the entire podium
choices.win: The speech becomes considerably less confident.
choices.lose: The podium's foundations have sponsors of their own.

onWin.memory: You intimidated your rival by lifting the podium.

onLose.memory: A sponsored podium defeated your backstage warm-up.

scenes.text: Your rival suggests sawing the trophy in half. The engraver refuses on artistic grounds. You need a joint ending with fewer metal filings.

choices.label: Pitch the Guild's first job-share hero contract
choices.win: Alternate weekends, shared expenses, separate memoirs. The engraver writes an ampersand.
choices.lose: The Guild tries to pay one salary. You both object at once.

onWin.memory: You designed a job-share Hero of the Year contract.

choices.label: Get matching signatures before anyone changes their mind
choices.win: Signed. The hairbrush serves as the official quill.
choices.lose: Your rival signs the hairbrush instead.

onWin.memory: Your joint hero contract was signed with a hairbrush quill.

scenes.text: The Guild has invited everyone you helped to give character references. Someone has reserved a large seat marked 'possible soup'.

choices.label: Let the witnesses describe what actually happened
choices.win: It is not flattering. It is specific. The audience believes every word.
choices.lose: A witness opens with 'technically nobody died'. A difficult start.

onWin.memory: Your clients gave painfully specific character references at the showdown.

choices.label: Check the witness queue for rival-sponsored actors
choices.win: Three actors admit it immediately. Their contracts include confession pay.
choices.lose: You eject an actual grateful client. They revise their reference.

onWin.memory: You exposed three rival-sponsored character witnesses.

finaleChoices.label: Present the joint Hero of the Year contract
finaleChoices.win: The Guild accepts. Two heroes, one trophy, absolutely incompatible office hours.
finaleChoices.lose: The Guild demands a probationary duel. Human resources are terrible.

onWin.memory: You and your rival became joint Heroes of the Year.

rivals.text: Your rival is physically blocking the quest route while a painter captures their 'spontaneous act of heroism'. The painter asks you to look more rescued.

choices.label: Charge a modelling fee and hold the pose
choices.win: You negotiate royalties. The painter titles it 'Hero With Expensive Witness'.
choices.lose: Your rival frames you as the problem being defeated.

onWin.memory: You billed your rival for posing in their heroic portrait.

choices.label: Pay for a quiet truce away from the painter
choices.hint: Remembered throughout this season; opens a showdown ending.
choices.win: A handshake behind the canvas. Neither of you is as confident off camera.
choices.lose: Talks fail.

onWin.memory: You made a private road truce with your rival.

choices.label: Duck under the canvas without entering the composition
choices.win: You pass unnoticed. Your rival rescues an empty patch of grass.
choices.lose: You trip into the perfect defeated-villain pose.

onWin.memory: Your rival's heroic portrait depicts the rescue of empty grass.

rivals.text: Your rival is alone on a milestone, struggling to open a lunch tin. The great rival of your season has been defeated by a small clip.

choices.label: Open it and agree never to mention this
choices.win: The tin opens. So does a guarded conversation about the pressure to be legendary.
choices.lose: Now neither of you can open it. A strangely intimate defeat.

onWin.memory: You opened your rival's lunch tin and promised discretion.

choices.label: Buy lunch for both of you
choices.hint: Renew or establish a truce that the showdown remembers.
choices.win: Two pies. No audience. It briefly feels like adventuring with a friend.
choices.lose: The pie shop has closed.

onWin.memory: You shared two quiet pies with your rival.

choices.label: Open it by demonstrating superior upper-body strength
choices.win: The clip yields. The soup travels a remarkable distance.
choices.lose: The tin is now angry at both of you.

onWin.memory: You launched your rival's lunch into the middle distance.

rivals.text: Your rival has a spare invitation to the trophy ceremony. It says '+1: formidable nemesis or equivalent'. The handwriting under 'equivalent' is hesitant.

choices.label: Accept as a formidable equivalent
choices.win: They smile before remembering not to. A real one, briefly.
choices.lose: You both deliver rehearsed threats over each other. Neither sounds convincing.

onWin.memory: You accepted your rival's ceremony invitation as a formidable equivalent.

choices.label: Read the invitation for hidden disqualification clauses
choices.win: The only condition is to wear shoes. You are already ahead.
choices.lose: The invitation bites. Security feature.

onWin.memory: You checked the ceremony rules and confirmed shoes were compulsory.

choices.label: Put the invitation somewhere nobody can steal it
choices.win: Safe inside your boot. The trophy ceremony now smells like determination.
choices.lose: You hide it so well the Guild briefly disqualifies you both.

onWin.memory: You stored your trophy-ceremony invitation inside your boot.
